The aphorism is often misunderstood because people take it literally, as a sweeping claim that status vanishes and everything becomes free contract. Maine meant something narrower: that the legal rights and duties of individuals, once fixed by their position in family groups, increasingly arise from individual agreement. His concept of status is also misrepresented, since modern law still assigns status-based rights and duties (for example to children, or employees under mandatory protections), and he described a historical tendency, not an inevitable or moral law.

CONFIDENCE: 72
